newsitem.title: GERMANY: Non-preferred Traub creditors to get no pay-out.
newsitem.headline: Non-preferred Traub creditors to get no pay-out.

text.p: The administrator of bankrupt German machine tool-maker Traub AG said on Tuesday that under an agreed takeover plan involving Esslingen-based Index-Werke no pay-out would be made to non-preferential creditors.

Speaking at a news briefing, the administrator, Volker Grub, added that Index had agreed to take over only the Traub assets. The existing Traub corporate entity would be liquidated and its shares remain valueless.

Grub said Index would take over Traub assets with effect backdated to March 1 and establish a new company for them. Some 450 Traub workers would be taken on by Index, compared to the 1,100 that were employed by Traub at its main plant late last year.
Staff made redundant will be allowed to draw their net income for a maximum period of six months.
Both Traub and Index are leading manufacturers of motorised lathes.

Index last year increased its turnover by 10 percent to 440 million marks ($261 million), with some 1,550 staff. Traub earlier this year initiated bankruptcy proceedings following the failure of efforts to scale back debt with creditors.
